name: Franco-Ontarians (Canada)
description: Two vertical halves: green at the hoist bearing a white fleur-de-lis, white at the fly bearing a green trillium.
history: Created by Gaétan Gervais and Michel Dupuis and first raised at the University of Sudbury on 25 September 1975; recognized as an official emblem of Ontario in 2001. The fleur-de-lis marks the French language, the trillium is Ontario's flower; green and white evoke summer and winter.
